transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Miguel Santos (Redwood SE), Tom Reynolds (Larkspur VP Platform), Priya Shah (Head of Data), Evan Li (SRE), Maya Ortiz (Security)

Summary:
Quick discovery to understand Larkspur's inference needs and whether Dedicated or Private deployment is needed; focus on reserved GPU capacity, burst handling, isolation/VPC, security (KMS/SOC2), and pilot benchmarks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Aisha from Redwood, epic to meet you all. We'll do a quick intro then dig into your workload and requirements. Miguel and I will take notes and follow up with pricing and security docs.
[00:14] Tom: Thanks Aisha. Tom here, VP of Platform at Larkspur. We run a few internal models today and are trying to decide if we go Redwood hosted or get dedicated capacity or even private. Main concerns are compliance and predictable cost.
[00:28] Miguel: Hi Tom, Miguel from Redwood, I focus on architecting Dedicated and Private deployments. Curious about throughput, latency SLOs, and data residency.
[00:42] Priya: Hi, Priya. Our main use cases are AML triage and customer support routing. Typical prompt sizes are 200-400 tokens, sometimes 1k for longer context. Peak QPS around 80-120 requests per second during morning batch windows, but most of the day it's 15-25 qps.
[01:05] Evan: And from infra side, we need isolation — no shared GPU pools that could leak logs. We'll want VPC peering and control plane separation.
[01:20] Maya: Security wise, SOC2 is table stakes, we also use GCP KMS and may need HSM for some keys. Data retention policy: PII must be purged within 24 hours unless encrypted and stored.
[01:40] Aisha: Great, that's helpful. Miguel, do you want to talk through Dedicated options and burst?
[01:45] Miguel: Sure. For Dedicated we offer reserved GPU pools — you pick a commit for number of GPUs and throughput. We support a burst buffer for spiky traffic: short-lived autoscaling into a shared burst pool or pre-purchased burst credits. The tradeoff is cost vs guaranteed capacity.
[02:10] Tom: Can you clarify how burst into shared pools works? We don't want noisy neighbors affecting latency.
[02:20] Miguel: Good question. Burst into the shared pool is prioritized but not isolated; we throttled by policy and have fallback model variants if a higher-tier model is constrained. If isolation is required, we recommend private or larger Dedicated commit to cover peaks. Also we can do guaranteed burst seats as an add-on which are isolated.
[02:45] Priya: How does the KV cache and prefix caching play into cost? Our models reuse a lot of contexts across requests.
[02:55] Miguel: We have automatic prefix/KV caching at the runtime level; for Dedicated you can configure longer-lived caches which reduces downstream cost. This is especially effective for repeated system prompts and retrieval-augmented calls.
[03:18] Evan: Network-wise, we need VPC peering with restricted egress. Will Redwood support VPC peering and single-tenant control plane?
[03:28] Miguel: Yes — Dedicated supports customer VPC peering and Private deployments provide an on-prem or VPC-isolated control plane. For sensitive workloads we often recommend Private with a customer-controlled control plane; that adds ops complexity but meets strict compliance.
[03:45] Tom: What's the expected latency for our 400-token prompts on Dedicated? We need p95 under 450ms if possible.
[03:55] Miguel: It depends on model and GPU type; with A100-class or newer and optimized kernels you'll typically see p95 in 300-500ms for 400-token generation on standard decoder-only models. Quantization and kernel selection also matter; we'll share performance profiles for the model you plan to run.
[04:20] Priya: We're evaluating open models — which ones do you recommend for cost vs quality?
[04:28] Miguel: We have a curated model catalog with verifed performance profiles. For bank-grade accuracy we usually suggest a 7B-13B tuned variant for many tasks, or larger when context length or reasoning demands it. We also support custom finetuned weights if you want to bring them.
[04:50] Tom: About data retention — do logs or request metadata leave our VPC?
[04:58] Miguel: For Dedicated with customer VPC peering, logs can be routed to your logging endpoints. For Hosted, we do collect telemetry for billing but you can opt for no retention. For Private, control plane sits in your environment and nothing leaves unless you configure exports.
[05:18] Maya: We need support for KMS and HSM. Do you integrate with GCP KMS and commonly used HSM providers?
[05:27] Miguel: Yes, we integrate with GCP KMS and AWS KMS; HSM integrations are supported for Private deployments. We'll include the KMS integration guide in the security pack.
[05:45] Evan: For the pilot — we want to run a 2-week benchmark with a subset of production traffic. How do we set that up and what telemetry can we get?
[05:53] Miguel: We can provision a pilot cluster in Dedicated mode with telemetry from the Redwood Console: token-level cost, latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards. We'll also provide tracing hooks and KV cache hit rates. The pilot can run with your request sampler; we recommend a 48-hour warmup followed by a 7-14 day steady run.
[06:20] Tom: Pricing — are there monthly commits and overage rates? We're trying to model budget for next quarter.
[06:28] Aisha: Yes, Dedicated is committed capacity with monthly/annual options. We provide tiers and there are burst credits/guaranteed burst seats as add-ons. Miguel will send a pricing spreadsheet with scenarios based on your peak/avg profile.
[06:45] Priya: For the commit sizing, if we have 120 QPS peaks, any rule of thumb for GPUs? We run models that cost about X tokens per request — sorry unclear — but mostly we need throughput.
[06:58] Miguel: Rule of thumb: a single A100-80GB-equivalent can handle roughy 20-40 concurrent streams depending on seq len and model. For 120 qps with 400-token prompts and average concurrency, you'd probably want a cluster sized for sustained 60-80 qps plus burst coverage. We'll run exact sizing in the pilot.
[07:25] Tom: What's the SLA for Dedicated?
[07:30] Aisha: We offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets for Dedicated depending on contract tier. Standard is 99.9% uptime; performance SLOs are specified in the contract for higher tiers.
[07:46] Maya: Audit logs — we need fine-grained audit trails for all requests and admin actions.
[07:54] Miguel: We capture admin action logs, route changes, and token-level traces that can be exported to your logging stack or stored in the control plane with retention policies. We'll include the retention options in the docs.
[08:12] Evan: Any limits on model size or custom kernels? We have a few finetuned 70B models in-house.
[08:22] Miguel: Dedicated supports a wide range; large models require more GPU memory and may be better on multi-GPU nodes or tensor-slicing. For 70B we often recommend multi-node configs with NVLink or equivalent. That's typically a Private or high-tier Dedicated deployment.
[08:50] Priya: If we start with Dedicated but later move to Private, how portable are configs and model artifacts?
[08:58] Miguel: Configs are portable — we use containerized runtimes and model artifacts can be migrated. Private requires some extra ops work for network and key management, but we help with the migration plan.
[09:18] Tom: For cost modeling, can you provide an example case — 10 A100-equivalents reserved vs pay-as-you-go?
[09:25] Aisha: We'll put together an example in the spreadsheet. High-level: reserved commits lower unit costs and provide predictability; pay-as-you-go or burst credits give flexibility but higher per-token price.
[09:40] Evan: On the networking side, we need to avoid cross-region egress — all infra must remain in us-west1. Is that supported?
[09:48] Miguel: Yes, region pinning is available for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we have regional endpoints but not guaranteed isolation in the same way.
[10:05] Maya: Any pen test or compliance workflows needed from our side?
[10:12] Miguel: We can coordinate a security review. We have SOC2 and ISO artifacts, and we can provide a scoping questionnaire for any pen test windows. For Private deployments usually customers run their own pen tests.
[10:30] Priya: What about automatic rollbacks or graceful degradation if your preferred model becomes unavailable?
[10:38] Miguel: We support routing policies with automated fallback to compatible model variants and graceful degradation strategies. For Dedicated you can pin model versions and define canary rollout policies.
[10:55] Tom: Are you able to run inside our air-gapped environment if needed?
[11:00] Miguel: Yes — Private on-prem packages are available for air-gapped deployments, though that extends lead time and requires some on-prem infra support.
[11:15] Aisha: Ok, to recap next steps: we'll send pricing and security pack, schedule pilot kickoff, and you provide traffic samples and SLOs. Anything else?
[11:24] Priya: Please include recommendations for quantization and kernel optimizations for our model family.
[11:30] Miguel: Will do — we'll include quantization profiles and expected quality/cost tradeoffs.
[11:36] Tom: Thanks all, let's aim to review the pricing by Friday.
[11:40] Aisha: Sounds good. I'll follow up with the spreadsheet and schedule. Thanks everyone.
[11:48] End of recording.

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-heard words ("verifed" instead of "verified", "noisy neighbors" transcribed correctly though), filler words present. Speaker labels mostly accurate though may show role in parentheses.
